long_biography.plain_text:
Raised in the Bronx, Maitland entered Columbia expecting to study medicine before choosing economics and finance. Internships opened a route to Wall Street, and Merrill Lynch's analyst programme led to convertible securities. He later headed convertible sales, helping introduce institutional investors to hybrid instruments that combined bond protection with equity participation.

In 1995, Maitland left Merrill to establish Advent around that specialised knowledge. The firm broadened from convertibles into high-yield credit, bank debt, closed-end funds and alternative strategies, while retaining capital-structure research as its core discipline. He continued to supervise the investment team and co-manage portfolios, and later codified the field in a book written with two Advent colleagues.
